hero: Informal businesses and jobs rebounded as November’s flash PMI showed factories gaining momentum and services slowing. India is weighing a rice export duty, the EU ambassador has flagged a possible mid-2027 start for the trade deal, and India and Nepal signed eight agreements. Karnataka mandated free menstrual products in schools, while an L&T group company secured a Chennai AI infrastructure order.

cards.brief: India’s November flash composite PMI reached 56.3. Manufacturing gained momentum and export orders recovered, while services activity and hiring weakened.
cards.mechanism: Stronger factory demand can lift the overall reading even when service firms and hiring lose momentum.
cards.watch: Watch whether the final November survey confirms the gap between manufacturing and services.

cards.brief: NSO reported that informal enterprises rose 9.2% from the previous quarter and employment rose 9.7% in the second quarter of FY27. Rural areas led the rebound after a sharp first-quarter decline.
cards.mechanism: A recovery among rural informal businesses can support household earnings and spending in local markets.
cards.watch: Watch whether rural enterprise and employment gains carry through to the next release.
cards.headline: India's informal sector rebounds in Q2FY27 led by rural recovery: NSO

cards.brief: EU Ambassador Jean-Eric Paquet said the India–EU trade deal could take effect by mid-2027. The agreement still requires European Parliament approval.
cards.mechanism: The approval timeline determines when eligible shipments can start claiming the deal’s tariff preferences.
cards.watch: Watch for a confirmed signing date and a timetable for the European Parliament vote.

cards.brief: The Economic Times reported that India is considering a 20% export duty on select rice varieties to improve domestic supply. The report said rising broken-rice prices have affected poultry and cattle-feed producers.
cards.mechanism: If imposed, a duty could make exports less attractive and leave more of the covered rice available to domestic buyers.
cards.watch: Watch for a formal notification specifying which varieties would face the duty and when it would begin.
cards.headline: India weighs 20% export duty on select rice varieties to boost domestic supply

claims.statement: The Economic Times reported that India is considering a 20% export duty on select rice varieties to improve domestic supply.
evidence: India weighs 20% export duty on select rice varieties to boost domestic supply

India is contemplating the imposition of export duties on specific rice varieties to improve domestic supplies. This measure aims to mitigate rising prices faced by consumers and industries in the local market. Although the export duty might slow rice exports, it is unlikely to halt shipments completely due to competitive pricing. The poultry and cattle feed sectors have been notably affected by the surge in broken rice prices.

cards.mechanism: Providing pads in school can lower the cost and access barriers students face during the school day.
cards.watch: Watch for school-level delivery schedules and how the state checks compliance.

catalysts.text: The Centre is scheduled to launch the fifth edition of the Nayi Chetna gender campaign on November 25.
catalysts.evidence: Centre to launch fifth edition of Nayi Chetna gender campaign on Nov 25

catalyst_review: The Nayi Chetna launch is explicitly dated November 25 and represents a distinct nationwide programme milestone. The Madurai restrictions are scheduled to expire on that date unless withdrawn earlier, but apply to a single local event. The exchange holiday, Motorola launch and relative Deepam reference point to November 24. Sugar officials meet November 27, Tata Sons and the Delhi toll comment deadline are November 30, and the summit, school admissions and trade signing preview fall in December. The remaining weekly calendar, parliamentary dates and court or policy previews provide no firm November 25 deliverable.
